name: awgraph
description: A code knowledge graph for agents: symbols, call paths and dependencies, served as the few chunks a task needs instead of a grep dump.
notes: Retrieval measured over 33 real commits: the task is a commit message with answer filenames stripped, the truth is the files that commit modified.
k is swept for BOTH retrievers, because k bounds grep's output too - sweeping it for one arm only manufactures a win, and an earlier published version did exactly that.

grep is the better FINDER at any matched k (1.000 at k=50 vs awgraph 0.939). The claim is cost: awgraph reaches the same 1.000 ceiling for 16x less context, and grep's 668k tokens/task at full recall does not fit most context windows.
awgraph's token counts are previews (signature + docstring + body excerpt); an agent reading its top hits in full pays more. grep's figure is whole files.
REFUTED: embedding coverage was not the gap - 33.3% -> 100% coverage moved recall@10 only 0.800 -> 0.803.

DID NOT WORK: naive graph-then-grep fusion scored 0.894 at 348,389 tokens, because a fallback keyed on result COUNT fires when the graph is confidently wrong and stays quiet when it is confidently right.
